children.text: insurance that covers therapy (not sure if this is available/useful)

rows.gap: The catalog counts mental-health providers, but does not measure how far they are, therapy costs, sliding-scale availability, or whether insurance covers care.
rows.title: Affordable, Insurance-Covered Therapy Access
rows.likely_source: NPI/CMS provider data and SAMHSA treatment directories for provider locations; provider and insurer listings for costs and coverage; ACS for general insurance coverage
rows.reason: Provider availability is partly represented, but affordability and practical access are not.

children.text: are mental health incidents tracked in police data

rows.gap: The existing measure covers frequent mental distress, not separate depression and anxiety statistics or mental-health-related police incidents.
rows.title: Depression, Anxiety, and Mental-Health Crisis Incidents
rows.likely_source: CDC PLACES and Chicago Health Atlas; Chicago Police Department calls-for-service data, if mental-health incidents are identifiable
rows.reason: Frequent mental distress is related, but it does not answer the specific condition and incident questions.

children.text: social listening / social media sentiment analysis

rows.gap: The catalog has modeled wellbeing estimates, but no measure derived from social-media posts or comparing sentiment across platforms.
rows.title: Ward-Level Social-Media Sentiment
rows.likely_source: Public platform APIs such as Bluesky's; platform-specific public data and location metadata
rows.reason: Existing happiness estimates are related to feelings but are not social-listening measures.

rows.gap: The catalog has modeled happiness estimates, but no Bluesky-derived sentiment measure; usable ward-level post locations may also be scarce.
rows.title: Bluesky Sentiment by Ward
rows.likely_source: Bluesky public API or firehose, if posts can be assigned reliable locations
rows.reason: Modeled happiness is a different data source and method from Bluesky sentiment analysis.

rows.gap: Existing measures estimate happiness from demographic circumstances, not from Google searches, local surveys, or quotes using the proposed GNH methodology.
rows.title: Search- or Survey-Based Wellbeing Signal
rows.likely_source: Google Trends; a Chicago resident survey for ward-level responses
rows.reason: The catalog covers related wellbeing concepts but not the proposed search-based or survey-based method.

rows.gap: Overdose deaths capture one severe outcome, but do not measure substance use prevalence, other substances, or access to prevention and treatment.
rows.title: Substance-Use Prevalence and Treatment Access
rows.likely_source: CDPH and Cook County overdose surveillance; Chicago Health Atlas; CDC PLACES for relevant substance-use estimates
rows.reason: The overdose-death measure is relevant but covers only a narrow part of substance use and its effects.

rows.title: Third places
rows.likely_source: Google Maps via Apify third-places sweeps
rows.reason: The published third-places measure counts gathering spaces such as cafés, bars and restaurants.

rows.gap: The existing measure covers gathering places open at 9pm on weekdays, not businesses generally open past 8pm.
rows.title: Businesses open past 8pm
rows.likely_source: Google Maps business listings and opening hours
rows.reason: Open Late is similar but uses a later cutoff and a narrower set of places.

rows.title: Coffee shops
rows.likely_source: OpenStreetMap / Overpass API; Chicago business licenses (BACP)
rows.reason: The catalog already counts coffee shops in the area.

rows.title: Bars
rows.likely_source: Google Maps via Apify third-places sweeps; Chicago business licenses (BACP)
rows.reason: Existing measures count dedicated bars and licensed taverns.

rows.title: Parks
rows.likely_source: OpenStreetMap / Overpass API
rows.reason: The catalog includes a direct count of mapped parks.

rows.gap: Existing measures cover commute mode and access to selected destinations, but not a composite score of how walkable the area is.
rows.title: Walkability score
rows.likely_source: Chicago open data and OpenStreetMap street, destination and transit networks
rows.reason: The related measures do not capture overall walkability as a score.

rows.gap: Existing measures cover bike-route supply, commute mode and crash harm, but not a composite measure of bikeability, including network comfort and access.
rows.title: Bikeability score
rows.likely_source: Chicago bike routes and traffic crash data; OpenStreetMap
rows.reason: The catalog has related cycling measures but no overall bikeability score.

rows.gap: A ward-level unemployment rate would add a direct labor-market measure; existing income and poverty measures do not show whether residents are unemployed.
rows.title: Unemployment rate
rows.likely_source: American Community Survey 5-year estimates
rows.reason: No catalog measure directly reports unemployment.

rows.gap: Existing measures cover specific neighbor contact, favors or modeled weekly socializing, but not a general measure of how often residents interact across their social circles.
rows.title: General social interaction frequency
rows.likely_source: A local resident survey; CPS Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement for limited related estimates
rows.reason: The available measures address only particular types or modeled frequencies of interaction.

rows.title: Neighborhood incomes
rows.likely_source: American Community Survey; IRS Statistics of Income
rows.reason: The catalog already reports household income and income per tax return.

rows.gap: A consumer price index would track price changes, which the existing income and rent measures do not. Public inflation data is not available at ward geography.
rows.title: Ward-level cost inflation
rows.likely_source: Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI for the Chicago-Naperville-Elgin metro area
rows.reason: The available CPI is regional rather than ward-level, and no existing measure tracks local inflation.

rows.gap: The catalog counts city-owned parcels, most of which are vacant, but misses vacant land owned by others.
rows.title: All vacant land, not just city-owned parcels
rows.likely_source: Cook County Assessor parcel records; Chicago City-Owned Land Inventory
rows.reason: The city-owned parcel measure is a useful proxy but does not cover all vacant land.

rows.gap: Existing measures cover rents and rent burden, but not other household costs such as food, utilities, or transportation.
rows.title: Non-housing household costs
rows.likely_source: American Community Survey; Bureau of Labor Statistics
rows.reason: The catalog covers housing costs but not the broader costs implied by the idea.

rows.gap: The catalog has no measure of current job vacancies; employment or business counts would not show openings.
rows.title: Job openings
rows.likely_source: Illinois Department of Employment Security labor-market data
rows.reason: No existing measure counts job vacancies, and public vacancy data is not plausibly available by ward.

rows.gap: A tax-burden measure would compare taxes paid with income or another household resource; the catalog has no tax measure.
rows.title: Household tax burden
rows.likely_source: Cook County Treasurer; Cook County Assessor; American Community Survey
rows.reason: Public property-tax and income records could support a ward-level measure, but the catalog has none.

rows.gap: Existing measures estimate landlord profit or absentee ownership, but do not directly report the share of neighborhood rent revenue captured by property owners.
rows.title: Share of rent captured by property owners
rows.likely_source: Cook County Assessor and Recorder records; American Community Survey
rows.reason: The landlord measures are close, but profit share and absentee ownership are not the same as rent share.

rows.gap: The catalog covers rent and income but not a broader household expense basket or overall cost-of-living index.
rows.title: Ward-level cost-of-living index
rows.likely_source: American Community Survey; Bureau of Labor Statistics
rows.reason: Existing housing-cost measures do not answer the broader cost-of-living idea.

rows.gap: The catalog counts or estimates permitted housing, not homes actually completed and added to the housing stock.
rows.title: Completed new housing units
rows.likely_source: Chicago Department of Buildings permits and certificates of occupancy
rows.reason: Permits are a close indicator but do not establish that housing was built.

rows.gap: No catalog measure estimates the costs of preparing and developing a lot; sale prices and zoning capacity are not development costs.
rows.title: Cost of developing a lot
rows.likely_source: Chicago Department of Buildings permits and fees; Cook County Assessor
rows.reason: The catalog has no measure of actual lot development costs.

rows.gap: Existing measures cover crime, modeled fear of walking at night, and serious traffic harms, but not a broader, clearly defined view of neighborhood safety.
rows.title: Broader neighborhood safety measure
rows.likely_source: Chicago Police Department; Chicago traffic crash data; Chicago Health Atlas
rows.reason: Several safety dimensions are live, but no single measure answers the broad idea as stated.

rows.text: access to resources (grocery stores, transit, noise, bike line)
rows.gap: The catalog covers grocery proximity, rail access, noise complaints, and bike-route supply, but not access to bus service or a combined resource-access measure.
rows.title: Bus transit access
rows.likely_source: Chicago Transit Authority bus stops and routes; Chicago Data Portal
rows.reason: Most listed examples have close measures, while bus access is the clear missing transit variant.

rows.gap: The existing measures count reported flooding complaints, not modeled inundation extent or depth using elevation data.
rows.title: LiDAR-based inundation risk
rows.likely_source: Cook County LiDAR; Chicago Department of Water Management; Metropolitan Water Reclamation District
rows.reason: Flooding complaints are a nearby indicator but do not model where water would inundate land.

rows.title: Insurance coverage
rows.likely_source: American Community Survey
rows.reason: The uninsured share directly indicates the share of residents without insurance coverage.

rows.gap: The existing measure counts mental-health providers, not general doctors or how far residents travel to reach one. A new measure could estimate distance to primary-care doctors.
rows.title: Distance to primary-care doctors
rows.likely_source: CMS National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES) provider locations
rows.reason: A nearby provider-count measure exists, but it does not answer distance to general doctors.

rows.title: Homicide rate
rows.likely_source: Chicago Police violence reduction victims data
rows.reason: The catalog already reports homicide victims per 10,000 residents.

rows.gap: Existing measures estimate leisure time and time poverty, but do not describe residents’ broader daily time use or provide observed local time-use data.
rows.title: Daily time use measured directly
rows.likely_source: American Time Use Survey (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics)
rows.reason: The catalog has modeled time-use indicators, but not a direct, comprehensive measure of local time use.

rows.gap: The existing measure covers distance to CTA rail, but not access to other transit such as bus stops.
rows.title: Distance to nearest transit stop
rows.likely_source: Chicago Transit Authority bus and rail stop locations
rows.reason: Distance to the nearest rail station is covered, but it does not represent access to transit generally.

rows.gap: Existing measures count child-care establishments per capita, but do not show residents’ proximity to centers or whether centers have available places.
rows.title: Distance to nearest child-care center
rows.likely_source: Illinois Department of Children and Family Services licensed child-care provider data
rows.reason: The catalog measures child-care supply, not geographic or usable access.

rows.title: Distance to a place of worship
rows.likely_source: OpenStreetMap / Overpass API
rows.reason: The existing measure estimates distance to the nearest place of worship.

rows.gap: Existing measures estimate happiness and whether life feels exciting, but do not capture whether residents feel a sense of purpose.
rows.title: Residents who feel a sense of purpose
rows.likely_source: Chicago Health Atlas / Healthy Chicago Survey, if a purpose question is available
rows.reason: Purpose is related to subjective wellbeing, but the catalog has no measure of purpose itself.

rows.gap: The existing measures cover faith institutions and places of worship, not faith-associated spaces or businesses that are not used for worship.
rows.title: Non-worship faith-associated spaces and businesses
rows.likely_source: OpenStreetMap / Overpass API; Chicago business licenses
rows.reason: Worship-place measures are adjacent, but the idea calls for a distinct category of non-worship sites.

rows.gap: The catalog has general historic-building and landmark counts, but no measure of the historical significance of faith-associated places; the idea's intended meaning also needs clarification.
rows.title: Historic significance of faith-associated places
rows.likely_source: Chicago Historic Resources Survey; Chicago Landmarks; National Register of Historic Places
rows.reason: General historic-site measures are related, but they do not isolate or define the faith-related historical dimension.

rows.gap: The existing measure covers distance to public schools, not schools of all types. Add private schools or clearly distinguish the school types covered.
rows.title: Distance to all schools
rows.likely_source: CPS and NCES school directories, including the Private School Universe Survey
rows.reason: The catalog measures distance to the nearest public school, but not schools generally.

rows.gap: These measures cover individual school outcomes and spending, but do not provide a user-friendly overall school rating. A new measure would need to define how ratings are constructed and presented.
rows.title: School quality ratings
rows.likely_source: Illinois Report Card / CPS
rows.reason: Existing school measures are related inputs, not a Zillow-style rating.

rows.gap: The existing measure reports only the share of adults with a bachelor's degree or higher. Add the distribution across highest education levels attained.
rows.title: Educational attainment by highest level
rows.likely_source: American Community Survey 5-year estimates
rows.reason: The catalog has a bachelor's-or-higher share, not attainment levels across the population.

rows.title: Voter participation rate
rows.likely_source: Chicago municipal election results; Chicago Board of Elections
rows.reason: The catalog already measures ballots cast as a share of registered voters.

rows.gap: The existing measure records whether participatory budgeting is used, not how many people vote or submit project ideas. A new measure would add those participation counts.
rows.title: Participatory budgeting votes and project ideas
rows.likely_source: UIC Great Cities Institute, Chicago ward records, and City of Chicago participatory budgeting records
rows.reason: The catalog covers the presence of participatory budgeting but not its participation or idea counts.

rows.gap: Existing measures cover 311 response time, attendance, and bills sponsored, but not 311 request volume or a defined way to assess overall alder performance. A scorecard would need clear, fair criteria for combining these dimensions.
rows.title: Alder service-delivery and legislative scorecard
rows.likely_source: Chicago 311 service requests and Chicago Councilmatic
rows.reason: Several listed performance dimensions are measured, but request volume and a defensible overall assessment are not.

rows.gap: The catalog has no measure of TIF revenue, spending, or results. A new measure could track how TIF funds are spent and define a transparent performance outcome.
rows.title: TIF spending and outcomes
rows.likely_source: City of Chicago TIF district financial reports and Department of Finance data
rows.reason: No catalog measure tracks TIF funds or evaluates their use.

rows.text: traffic study data on the transportation website (CDOT/ Illinois DOT)
rows.gap: The catalog has traffic proximity and crash measures, but not traffic-study counts such as vehicle volumes or speeds. A new measure could summarize CDOT or IDOT traffic study data by ward.
rows.title: Traffic volumes and speeds from traffic studies
rows.likely_source: Chicago CDOT traffic counts and Illinois DOT traffic count data
rows.reason: Existing traffic-related measures cover exposure and crashes, not the traffic-study data requested.

rows.text: gentrification / turnover of homes, neighborhood changes
rows.gap: These measures show related sales, ownership, business, and rent changes, but none directly measures residential turnover or displacement and neighborhood change as a whole.
rows.title: Residential turnover and neighborhood change
rows.likely_source: Cook County Assessor parcel sales; ACS; Chicago business licenses (BACP)
rows.reason: Several existing measures capture facets of neighborhood change but not the stated combined concept.

rows.text: rate of change in property taxes
rows.gap: The catalog has no measure of property-tax bills or how they change over time; property assessments and landlord estimates are not tax changes.
rows.title: Property tax change rate
rows.likely_source: Cook County Treasurer property tax bills; Cook County Assessor
rows.reason: No existing measure tracks property-tax amounts or their rate of change.

rows.gap: Existing place and historic-building counts do not measure residents’ perceptions of beauty; a new measure would need a defined rating approach.
rows.title: Neighborhood beauty rating
rows.likely_source: Google Street View imagery; resident survey
rows.reason: Beauty is a subjective concept not measured by any catalog indicator.

rows.gap: The catalog counts surveyed historic buildings and designated landmarks, but does not classify architectural styles across the building stock.
rows.title: Architectural style inventory
rows.likely_source: Chicago Historic Resources Survey; Cook County Assessor
rows.reason: Existing historic-building inventories are related but do not describe styles across buildings generally.

rows.gap: Transit entries and Divvy trips are activity proxies, not counts of people walking through neighborhood streets and commercial corridors.
rows.title: Pedestrian foot traffic
rows.likely_source: Chicago Department of Transportation pedestrian counts; Chicago Data Portal
rows.reason: Existing mobility measures miss direct counts of pedestrian activity.

rows.text: well-maintainedness of properties using google street map views
rows.gap: Violations and complaints capture reported or cited problems, not the visible upkeep of properties in street imagery.
rows.title: Visible property maintenance
rows.likely_source: Google Street View imagery; Chicago Department of Buildings
rows.reason: Code records are related proxies but do not rate visible property condition.

rows.text: chain vs non-chain percentage of businesses
rows.gap: Existing chain shares cover restaurants and food stores, but not the full range of businesses in a ward.
rows.title: Chain share across all businesses
rows.likely_source: Chicago business licenses (BACP)
rows.reason: The catalog measures chain status for food businesses, not businesses overall.

rows.text: survey question: comfortable asking for a stick of butter from a neighbor
rows.gap: Neighbor favor exchange and contact are related, but do not directly measure whether someone feels comfortable asking a neighbor for a small favor.
rows.title: Comfort asking neighbors for small favors
rows.likely_source: CPS Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement; Chicago Health Atlas
rows.reason: Existing neighbor measures do not capture comfort asking for help.

rows.text: survey question: trust of your neighbors
rows.gap: The catalog has modeled generalized trust and a social-cohesion proxy, but not direct trust in one’s neighbors.
rows.title: Trust in neighbors
rows.likely_source: Chicago Health Atlas / Healthy Chicago Survey; General Social Survey
rows.reason: Generalized trust and cohesion are not the same as neighbor-specific trust.

rows.gap: The catalog does not measure local meetup groups, events, or platform activity; venue and park-program counts do not show whether people organize or attend meetups.
rows.title: Community meetup activity
rows.likely_source: Meetup.com public event listings; Chicago Park District and Chicago Public Library event listings
rows.reason: No current measure captures organized meetup activity or use of a meetup platform.

rows.text: residential rootedness (how long have they lived where they live, ACS has this?)
rows.gap: No catalog measure reports how long residents have lived in their current homes; ACS tenure-duration data could support a new ward-level measure.
rows.title: Residential tenure duration
rows.likely_source: American Community Survey 5-year estimates (table B25038)
rows.reason: The catalog has no measure of residents’ length of residence.

rows.text: Institutional trust (GSS, Confidence in institutions, generalized trust)
rows.gap: The existing modeled measure covers generalized trust, but not confidence in institutions such as government, police, or media.
rows.title: Confidence in institutions
rows.likely_source: General Social Survey; small-area estimates using ACS covariates
rows.reason: The generalized-trust part is represented, while institutional confidence is missing.

rows.text: Neighborliness / mutual aid (CPS CEV - Informal helping, favors for neighbors, neighbor contact)
rows.gap: The catalog covers neighbor contact, exchanged favors, and collective action, but not informal helping more broadly.
rows.title: Informal neighbor help beyond favors and contact
rows.likely_source: CPS Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement; ACS covariates
rows.reason: Existing neighbor measures cover several listed variants but not informal help as a broader category.

rows.text: cook county recorder of deeds - real estate transfers (pdfs for each contract)
rows.gap: The catalog reports annual sale dollars, but not a count or accessible record-level view of real-estate transfers and their deeds or contracts.
rows.title: Real estate transfer records and counts
rows.likely_source: Cook County Clerk Recorder of Deeds; Cook County Assessor parcel sales
rows.reason: Recorded sale dollars are related but do not provide the transfer records or counts described.

rows.title: Distance to nearest park
rows.likely_source: Chicago Park District parks data / mapped park locations
rows.reason: The catalog already measures distance to the nearest park.

rows.gap: The existing measure estimates fear of walking near home at night, not safety within parks. A park-specific measure could use incidents in park areas and/or park conditions such as lighting.
rows.title: Safety within parks
rows.likely_source: Chicago Police Department crime records and Chicago Park District park data
rows.reason: A general perceived-safety estimate is related but does not assess safety in parks.

rows.gap: Existing measures cover city-owned parcels or cleanup requests, not all vacant lots. A new measure could identify vacant parcels regardless of ownership.
rows.title: All vacant lots
rows.likely_source: Cook County Assessor parcel data and Chicago City-Owned Land Inventory
rows.reason: The catalog has proxies but does not count vacant lots across all ownership.

rows.gap: The existing measure covers expected fear of walking alone at night near home; a broader measure could capture safety perceptions across places, times, or situations.
rows.title: Broader perceived safety
rows.likely_source: CDPH Healthy Chicago Survey / Chicago Health Atlas
rows.reason: A modeled nighttime-walking fear measure covers only one aspect of perceived safety.

rows.gap: The existing measure covers historically elevated lead in park fountains, not lead in park soil, play areas, or other park features.
rows.title: Lead in park soil and play areas
rows.likely_source: Chicago Park District and CDPH lead-testing records
rows.reason: The fountain measure addresses only one potential source of lead in parks.

rows.title: Sunlight access
rows.likely_source: Sunscore / Cook County LiDAR
rows.reason: The catalog measures annual sunlight access and seasonal sunlight variants.

rows.gap: The existing measure is distance to the shoreline, not distance to a publicly accessible lakefront entrance or access point.
rows.title: Distance to public lakefront access
rows.likely_source: Chicago Park District lakefront access data / OpenStreetMap
rows.reason: Shoreline proximity does not show whether residents can readily reach public access points.

rows.title: Language spoken at home
rows.likely_source: American Community Survey 5-year estimates
rows.reason: The catalog already measures home-language variety and the share speaking a non-English language at home.

rows.gap: A museum count does not show how accessible museums are to residents. A new measure could estimate distance or travel access to nearby museums.
rows.title: Distance to nearby museums
rows.likely_source: OpenStreetMap and City of Chicago museum locations
rows.reason: The catalog counts museums but does not measure residents’ access to them.

rows.gap: The arts-and-culture places count does not specifically capture public artworks. A new measure could count mapped public art installations, with a clear scope for what qualifies.
rows.title: Public art installations
rows.likely_source: City of Chicago Public Art Collection
rows.reason: A general arts-and-culture count is related, but it does not measure public artworks specifically.
